# Inputs that must NOT be flagged as secret material.

# Format: <category><TAB><text>. Lines starting with # are comments.
#
# The point of this file is the `questionnaire-terse` block. 108 of 153 words a wallet
# questionnaire would plausibly use are in the BIP-39 English wordlist (71%) — it is a
# list of ordinary English nouns and verbs, which is exactly the register these answers
# are written in. Prose is protected by function words (`the`, `and`, `of`, `to`, `a`,
# `is`, `in`, `my`), none of which are in the wordlist because it has no word shorter
# than three letters. Terse note-style answers drop those function words, which is what
# makes them the worst case for the density rule and the reason this block is the
# largest one here.
#
# Adding samples here is how a reviewer attacks the thresholds. Anything added must be
# something a real user could plausibly type.

# --- Comma-separated keyword lists. Same failure class as questionnaire-terse: these
# --- DO fire, and no threshold can stop them. `home safe, office safe, deposit box,
# --- metal plate, paper copy, spare device` is 12 tokens, 12 wordlist words, run 12,
# --- density 1.00 — the exact signature of a 12-word seed phrase. Measured, not asserted.
